title: Hiring subsidy
summary: Pays part of the wage for each new local hire during their first year.

how: Town staff design the subsidy and propose its budget.
Residents comment at a public hearing.
Town Council votes on the budget that funds it.

evidence.claim: Hiring credits cost roughly $9,100-$75,000 per job actually created
evidence.source: Neumark (2013), Journal of Policy Analysis and Management, via PPIC

pros: Pays for some local hires that would not have happened otherwise.
The added jobs raise spending at local businesses.
cons: Part of the money pays for hires that would have happened anyway: $9,100-$75,000 per job actually created in the study cited.
More jobs in Town add to demand for homes.
